chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from his father, raising it (to the Imam), said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said in one of his speeches: 'The wild beasts, their keenness is their bellies, and the women, their keenness is the men'.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hadith about women's keenness being men?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) draws a parallel between the dominant instinct of wild beasts (hunger) and women (marriage/desire), highlighting the natural inclination towards union. This hadith is frequently cited in Shia jurisprudence and theology to underscore the importance of marriage as a means of fulfilling innate human needs and maintaining social stability. The comparison emphasizes that just as beasts are driven by physical sustenance, women are naturally inclined towards the companionship and protection offered through marriage.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhour, from his father, raising it, said,
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said in one of his<sup>asws</sup> speeches that the wild animal, their keenness is their bellies, and the women, their keenness is the men’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Jumhur from his father in a marfu’ manner who has said the following: “’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in certain parts of his speech has said, ‘The ambition of beasts is to fill their stomach, and the ambition of women is to find men.’”
